title: Waypoint Woods
tagline: Follow Ranger Rowan along forest trails where Kit plans each step to a goal: how a program searches for, describes and guesses its way to a plan.

funFacts.text: STRIPS, the way of writing actions that most planning languages grew from, was developed in 1971 at SRI International.
The planning language PDDL was first developed in 1998, mainly so that an international planning competition could be held.
The FF planner, which guesses distance by ignoring what each action deletes, was the most successful automatic planner at the AIPS-2000 planning competition.
Manhattan distance is named after the grid of streets in Manhattan: it adds up the blocks you must walk along rows and columns.

starRules: 3 stars: no mistakes and no hints. 2 stars: up to 2 mistakes. 1 star: you finished.
